what_is_it.heading: STIs in plain terms
what_is_it.lede: Sexually transmitted infections are passed from one person to another during sex — vaginal, anal, or oral. They are very common, often have no symptoms, and most are easily treated when caught early.
paragraphs: Bacterial STIs (chlamydia, gonorrhoea, syphilis, trichomoniasis) are curable with a course of antibiotics. Viral STIs (herpes, HPV, HIV, hepatitis B) are managed long-term but not cured by treatment. Either way, testing is what makes treatment possible.

Most STIs have no obvious symptoms — particularly in women. Left untreated, they can cause infertility, pregnancy complications, and increase the risk of getting or passing on HIV. They are not a sign of bad behaviour. They are a sign of a normal sex life and a worth-having test.

items.headline: Often silent
items.body: Most STIs cause no symptoms at all — especially in women. Testing is the only reliable way to know.

items.headline: Free testing
items.body: Every government clinic offers free, confidential STI testing and treatment. No appointment, no medical aid.

items.headline: Most are curable
items.body: Chlamydia, gonorrhoea, syphilis, and trichomoniasis are all cured with a short course of antibiotics or one injection.

items.headline: Treat together
items.body: If you have an STI, recent partners need treatment too — even if they feel fine. Otherwise you will pass it back and forth.

pull_quote.text: An STI test is one of the most caring things you can do — for yourself, for the person you sleep with, and for any future partners. It is free and takes minutes.

signs.heading: What you might notice — and what you usually won't
signs.lede: Most STIs are silent. When symptoms appear, they vary depending on which infection you have. The same signs can mean different things — only a test can tell.

items.title: Unusual discharge
items.description: From the vagina, penis, or anus. May be cloudy, yellow, green, smelly, or just different from usual. Common in chlamydia, gonorrhoea, trichomoniasis.

items.title: Pain or burning
items.description: When urinating, during sex, or in the lower abdomen. Sometimes mistaken for a urinary tract infection.

items.title: Sores, bumps, or rash
items.description: On the genitals, anus, mouth, or hands. May or may not be painful. Common in herpes, syphilis, HPV.

items.title: Less obvious signs
items.description: Sore throat (oral gonorrhoea), swollen glands, flu-like illness (acute HIV), unusual bleeding between periods (cervical infection).

spreads.heading: How STIs spread — and how they don't
yes: Vaginal, anal, or oral sex without a condom
Sharing sex toys without cleaning or covering them
Skin-to-skin genital contact (HPV, herpes — even with a condom)
Mother to baby during pregnancy, birth, or breastfeeding (some STIs)
no: Hugging, holding hands, or kissing (for most STIs)
Sharing food, drinks, plates, or cutlery
Toilets, swimming pools, baths, or showers
Casual contact at work, school, or in public

myths.heading: What is true and what is not

items.myth: If they look healthy, they don't have an STI.
items.fact: Most STIs cause no visible signs. You cannot tell by looking at someone — including yourself. Testing is the only reliable way.

items.myth: You can't get an STI from oral sex.
items.fact: Many STIs spread through oral sex — gonorrhoea, chlamydia, syphilis, herpes, HPV. Condoms and dental dams reduce the risk.

items.myth: Condoms protect against every STI 100% of the time.
items.fact: Condoms are highly effective against most STIs when used correctly every time. Skin-to-skin STIs like HPV and herpes can still spread from areas not covered.

items.myth: If I was cured once, I am immune.
items.fact: You can get the same bacterial STI again after treatment. Re-testing 3 months after treatment is recommended for chlamydia and gonorrhoea.

prevention.heading: How to protect yourself
prevention.lede: Most STIs are preventable with a few simple habits. None of them require giving up sex — just having it with more awareness.

items.title: Condoms every time
items.description: Male or female condoms, used correctly from start to finish. Free at every clinic, many pharmacies, even some petrol stations.

items.title: HPV vaccine
items.description: Free in SA for girls in Grade 5 and now boys in many provinces. Protects against cervical cancer, genital warts, and other cancers.

items.title: Test before new partners
items.description: Test before sex with a new partner, ideally together. Free, fast, confidential. Most clinics give results in 15 minutes for HIV.

items.title: PrEP for HIV
items.description: A daily pill that prevents HIV. Free at clinics. Useful for people at higher risk — frequent new partners, partner with HIV, sex workers.

items.title: Get tested
items.description: Walk into any government clinic. Ask for a full STI screen — HIV, syphilis, gonorrhoea, chlamydia. Most results within minutes to days.

items.title: If positive — start treatment same day
items.description: Bacterial STIs are usually cured with a short course of antibiotics or a single injection. Take everything as prescribed.

items.title: Tell your recent partners
items.description: Anyone you have had sex with in the last 6 months needs to be tested. The clinic can help you tell them anonymously if needed.

items.title: No sex while being treated
items.description: Wait until the clinic says you are clear. Otherwise you will pass it back to the partner you just treated.

items.title: Re-test in 3 months
items.description: Bacterial STIs can come back if a partner was not treated. A follow-up test confirms the infection is gone.

get_help.heading: Where to go
get_help.lede: STI testing is free, fast, and confidential at every government clinic. No medical aid, no judgement, no questions you don't want to answer.
